name: Blinded
desc: - A blinded creature can't see and automatically fails any ability check that requires sight.
- Attack rolls against the creature have advantage, and the creature's attack rolls have disadvantage.
content: The condition known as Blinded renders a creature unable to see, causing automatic failure on ability checks that require sight. In addition, attacks against a blinded creature have advantage, while the creature's own attack rolls suffer from disadvantage. This condition can significantly impact combat and skill checks, making it a crucial factor to consider in various scenarios.

name: Deafened
desc: - A deafened creature can't hear and automatically fails any ability check that requires hearing.
content: Deafened: A condition where a creature can't hear, resulting in automatic failure of ability checks requiring hearing.

name: Incapacitated
desc: - An incapacitated creature can't take actions or reactions.
content: Incapacitated: An incapacitated creature in this state is unable to take actions or reactions.

name: Grappled
desc: - A grappled creature's speed becomes 0, and it can't benefit from any bonus to its speed.
- The condition ends if the grappler is incapacitated (see the condition).
- The condition also ends if an effect removes the grappled creature from the reach of the grappler or grappling effect, such as when a creature is hurled away by the thunderwave spell.
content: The "Grappled" condition occurs when a creature's speed becomes 0 and it loses the ability to benefit from speed bonuses. This condition ends if the grappler is incapacitated or if the grappled creature is moved out of reach. Being grappled restricts movement and can be a hindrance in combat situations, affecting the creature's ability to maneuver and escape.

name: Frightened
desc: - A frightened creature has disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while the source of its fear is within line of sight.
- The creature can't willingly move closer to the source of its fear.
content: The condition Frightened imposes disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls for a creature when the source of its fear is within line of sight. Additionally, the creature is unable to willingly move closer to the source of its fear. This condition can have a significant impact on a creature's performance in combat or other situations where bravery and courage are required.

name: Invisible
desc: - An invisible creature is impossible to see without the aid of magic or a special sense. For the purpose of hiding, the creature is heavily obscured. The creature's location can be detected by any noise it makes or any tracks it leaves.
- Attack rolls against the creature have disadvantage, and the creature's attack rolls have advantage.
content: The condition "Invisible" renders a creature unseen without magical assistance or special senses, causing it to be heavily obscured for hiding purposes. Detection of the creature's location is possible through noise or tracks. In combat, attacks against the invisible creature have disadvantage, while its own attacks have advantage.

name: Paralyzed
desc: - A paralyzed creature is incapacitated (see the condition) and can't move or speak.
- The creature automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws.
- Attack rolls against the creature have advantage.
- Any attack that hits the creature is a critical hit if the attacker is within 5 feet of the creature.
content: Paralyzed is a condition where a creature is unable to move or speak, automatically failing Strength and Dexterity saving throws, while also granting attackers advantage on their rolls. Additionally, any attack hitting the paralyzed creature within 5 feet is considered a critical hit.

name: Charmed
desc: - A charmed creature can't attack the charmer or target the charmer with harmful abilities or magical effects.
- The charmer has advantage on any ability check to interact socially with the creature.
content: Charmed condition: A creature affected by the Charmed (charmed) condition is unable to attack or harm the charmer and grants the charmer advantage on social interaction ability checks with the creature.

name: Poisoned
desc: - A poisoned creature has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.
content: The Poisoned condition causes a creature to have disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks. This condition is represented by the index "poisoned" and has a unique ID of "65f4e07d16025f62502809f5". You can find more information about the Poisoned condition by visiting the provided URL "/api/conditions/poisoned".

name: Petrified
desc: - A petrified creature is transformed, along with any nonmagical object it is wearing or carrying, into a solid inanimate substance (usually stone). Its weight increases by a factor of ten, and it ceases aging.
- The creature is incapacitated (see the condition), can't move or speak, and is unaware of its surroundings.
- Attack rolls against the creature have advantage.
- The creature automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws.
- The creature has resistance to all damage.
- The creature is immune to poison and disease, although a poison or disease already in its system is suspended, not neutralized.
content: The "Petrified" condition occurs when a creature is transformed into a solid, usually stone, rendering it incapacitated, immobile, and unaware of its surroundings. While petrified, the creature's weight increases tenfold, it ceases to age, and all attack rolls against it have advantage. Additionally, the creature automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws, but gains resistance to all damage and becomes immune to poison and disease (though any existing poison or disease remains suspended).

name: Stunned
desc: - A stunned creature is incapacitated (see the condition), can't move, and can speak only falteringly.
- The creature automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws.
- Attack rolls against the creature have advantage.
content: The Stunned condition renders a creature incapacitated, unable to move, and only able to speak falteringly. While under this condition, the creature automatically fails saving throws for Strength and Dexterity, making it vulnerable to attacks which have advantage.

name: Restrained
desc: - A restrained creature's speed becomes 0, and it can't benefit from any bonus to its speed.
- Attack rolls against the creature have advantage, and the creature's attack rolls have disadvantage.
- The creature has disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws.
content: The restrained condition renders a creature immobile, reducing its speed to 0 and nullifying any speed bonuses. Furthermore, attacks against the creature have advantage while its own attack rolls suffer from disadvantage. In addition, the creature's Dexterity saving throws are made with disadvantage.

name: Prone
desc: - A prone creature's only movement option is to crawl, unless it stands up and thereby ends the condition.
- The creature has disadvantage on attack rolls.
- An attack roll against the creature has advantage if the attacker is within 5 feet of the creature. Otherwise, the attack roll has disadvantage.
content: Prone condition: A creature affected by prone can only crawl or stand up to end the condition, suffering disadvantage on attack rolls and granting advantage to attackers within 5 feet while imposing disadvantage on attacks made from further away.

name: Unconscious
desc: - An unconscious creature is incapacitated (see the condition), can't move or speak, and is unaware of its surroundings.
- The creature drops whatever it's holding and falls prone.
- The creature automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws.
- Attack rolls against the creature have advantage.
- Any attack that hits the creature is a critical hit if the attacker is within 5 feet of the creature.
content: The Unconscious condition renders a creature incapacitated, unable to move, speak, or be aware of its surroundings. This state causes the creature to drop held items, fall prone, and automatically fail Strength and Dexterity saving throws. Additionally, attackers have advantage on rolls against the creature, and any hits within 5 feet are considered critical hits.

name: Exhaustion
desc: Some special abilities and environmental hazards, such as starvation and the long-term effects of freezing or scorching temperatures, can lead to a special condition called exhaustion. Exhaustion is measured in six levels. An effect can give a creature one or more levels of exhaustion, as specified in the effect's description.
1 - Disadvantage on ability checks
2 - Speed halved
3 - Disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws
4 - Hit point maximum halved
5 - Speed reduced to 0
6 - Death
If an already exhausted creature suffers another effect that causes exhaustion, its current level of exhaustion increases by the amount specified in the effect's description.

A creature suffers the effect of its current level of exhaustion as well as all lower levels. For example, a creature suffering level 2 exhaustion has its speed halved and has disadvantage on ability checks.
An effect that removes exhaustion reduces its level as specified in the effect's description, with all exhaustion effects ending if a creature's exhaustion level is reduced below 1.
Finishing a long rest reduces a creature's exhaustion level by 1, provided that the creature has also ingested some food and drink.
content: Exhaustion is a special condition that can be caused by certain abilities or environmental hazards, resulting in six levels of effects. These effects include disadvantage on ability checks, halved speed, disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws, halved hit point maximum, reduced speed to 0, and ultimately death. When a creature suffers additional exhaustion, its current level increases accordingly. Each level of exhaustion brings cumulative effects, with the highest level impacting all lower levels. Exhaustion can be removed by specific effects, with all levels disappearing if reduced below 1. Long rest, combined with food and drink intake, can decrease exhaustion by 1 level.
